statement: An ordinary Dirichlet series convergent in some right half-plane, meromorphic on C with finitely many poles, obeying Burnol strip bound O(exp(exp(epsilon|s|))) for every epsilon>0 in every finite strip, and exact conductor-one zeta self-dual FE, is a_1 zeta(s).
hypotheses: Integer frequencies n^(-s), finite poles, exact gamma Γ(s/2)π^(-s/2), sign+1; growth as stated, all constants allowed to depend on strip and epsilon.
evidence: PAPER-HC002 Theorem1 and Corollary2, pp2–3; proof pp7–10

statement: For normalized Bessel/quartet F_T, L_T=F_T π^(s/2)/[(s−1)Γ(1+s/2)] has only a simple pole at1 of residue2, has finite order after pole removal, satisfies exact zeta FE, but L_T(s)~[(2π)^(1/4)/D_T]s^(7/4) on the positive real axis. Hence it is not an ordinary Dirichlet series convergent in any right half-plane.

Knopp R(z)=π^(−z)Γ(z)φ(z), R(z)=R(1/2−z), with ordinary φ(z)=sum a_n n^(−z), becomes conventional zeta completion for F(s)=φ(s/2), whose frequencies are sqrt(n). Requiring F itself to be ordinary is a stronger assumption.
hypotheses: Exact change of variables s=2z. No infinite-series reordering is needed.

statement: For integer q>=2, f(s)=zeta(s)/[(1−q^(2−s))(1−q^(1+s))] satisfies exact zeta FE and has an ordinary DS absolutely convergent for Re(s)>2, but infinitely many simple poles at s=2+2πik/logq.
hypotheses: Classical nonvanishing of zeta for Re(s)>1 from its absolutely convergent Euler product. Infinite-pole example, not a finite-pole converse exception.

statement: If the tempered even integer-supported measure D=sum a_n(delta_n+delta_(-n)) has Fourier(D)−D quasi-homogeneous, then all a_n are equal. Combined with the moderate Mellin dictionary this proves the self-dual ordinary-series converse.
hypotheses: Tempered D, ordinary integer frequencies, quasi-homogeneous even difference. No positivity or Euler product needed.

statement: For every c>0 and nonzero polynomial P of integer degree d, standard uncompletion of P(s−1/2)K_((s−1/2)/2)(c) is not an ordinary Dirichlet series convergent in any right half-plane. Its positive-real asymptotic is p_d c^(1/4)(2π/c)^(σ/2)σ^(d−9/4); a first nonzero ordinary coefficient would require d=9/4.
hypotheses: Fixed c and P; standard Γ(s/2)π^(−s/2) completion with s(s−1)/2 factor; nonzero constant normalization allowed. No assertion about nonpolynomial modifications or sums of shifted Bessel orders.
